# smol-loop

This is a workflow for making your code changes more correct before (or
sometimes after) filing a pull request. tl;dr - use subagents to review
your code in a loop.

Make the most minimal possible changes to appease the "minion" reviewers. Be careful
of scope creep and don't be scared to push back.

"Minion(s)" = GPT 6 Luna or Haiku 5.5 models

GPT models are generally better at backend work, computer use/browser use, and being somewhat thourghough while Haiku is generally better(somewhat) at UI and writing cleaner, nicer to maintain code. Take this with a pinch of salt but don't waste your time trying to test out each model for every task and round you do because that's frivolous.

## Budget

- Default: 3 rounds total. Round 1 is full. Later rounds check only
  changed code and open findings.
- Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or
  state/concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open with evidence. Or when
  the user asks.
- Stop early if a round returns only nits. Declined nits and comment,
  doc, or format-only fixes need no new round.
- One reviewer only. "Minions" must not start subagents or reviewers.
- Keep a ledger: id, severity, outcome, usage if returned. Never guess it.

## 1. Scope

Run `git status --short`. Do not stash, discard, or include unrelated
changes. Limit review to the change paths if they separate cleanly.
Otherwise stop and ask.

Find the base after `git fetch origin`:

- PR: `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,headRefOid`. Check out the branch
  only if clean. Confirm `HEAD` is the PR head, or ahead only by this
  change. Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`.
- Local: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. No remote: a base
  the user names, or `HEAD` for uncommitted changes only.

The change is base to working tree in those paths, with untracked files.
Use one diff command all rounds. State intent and out-of-scope in 1-2
sentences. Run covering checks. Do not send code this change breaks. Note
missing or pre-failing checks in the brief.

## 2. Start a "minion"

In T3, call `orchestrator_capabilities`. Pick the latest "minion" model unless the user
named a version. Do not hardcode an ID. Record provider, model, and effort
only if exposed. Use `delegate_task` every round (`role: "review"`,
`mode: "async"`). Save `taskId`. New `clientRequestId` per round.
`childThreadId` is storage, not the next target. Do not use
`t3_thread_send`, `create_threads`, or `t3_thread_launch` for review.

If T3 tools are not listed, try one direct capability call. Outside T3, use
a native "minion" subagent and keep its ID. In Claude Code, use a custom subagent
only if it is set up to run "minion". If no route runs "minion", report the blocker. Do
not substitute a model.

Do not edit scoped files while review runs. Wait for the notice. Do not
poll or start a second reviewer. Timeout, error, or no reply is not
approval. On failure, cancel, verify stop, restart with the ledger.

Round 1 brief (T3 children get no history):

```
Review only. Do not edit, commit, push, comment on PRs, or start subagents.
Repo: <abs path> Base: <sha> Intent: <intent> Out of scope: <scope> Checks: <results>
See: git diff <base> [-- <paths>]; git status --short (read untracked).
Read surrounding code. Find bugs, broken callers, mismatch with intent.
Skip style unless it hides a bug. Hold to the smallest change. Flag code,
tests, or guards the intent does not need. Other paths, rare cases, small
perf, extra compat: nits.
blocker = intended case wrong. should = real bug callers will hit, in intent. nit = rest.
Reply:
VERDICT: APPROVE or CHANGES
S1 [blocker|should|nit] <file>:<line> <claim>. Fix: <suggestion> (stable ids)
```

## 3. Answer findings

Check each finding and severity yourself. Another path, rare case, or
small cost is a nit, whatever label it came with.

- Agree: smallest fix. Prefer delete or narrow over new lock, cache,
  helper, or option. Fix the case that happened. Add one focused test
  that fails without the fix, if intent needs it.
- Disagree: say why, with evidence (file:line, test, output).
- Out of scope or nit: decline in one line. List as follow-up.

Update the ledger. Re-run checks and `git diff --shortstat <base>`. If
review grew the diff, cut first. Do not agree just to end the loop.

## 4. Next round

Start one only if budget remains and a blocker or should is open, behavior code
changed, or approval does not cover the current behavior diff. Use a fresh
`delegate_task` in T3, or follow up the saved native ID. Send the round 1 brief,
the ledger (`fixed:` / `disagree:` / `declined:` + evidence), the same base
diff, and the change since last round. Tell the "minion": open ids and changed code only.
Mark each old id `resolved` or `still open: <reason>`.

## 5. Stop and ship

Agreed: APPROVE on the current behavior diff, no blocker or should open,
no concern of your own. Stuck: an item stays disputed after two replies,
or budget ends. Show both sides in 2-3 lines each. The user decides.
Budget end is not approval.

Do not push during the loop. Push after agreement only if the user asked
to push, ship, or update the PR. If you push to a PR, add above the model
blurb:

`Reviewed with smol-loop: <N> rounds with <model>. Minion verdict: approved`.

Add `on <effort>` only if verified.

Report: rounds, model, what the "minion(s)" changed, diff size before/after, fixed and
declined findings with reasons, usage if exposed (else say not), pushed or not.

# Full Stop

Do the same work as `full-send`, but stop with the PR ready for the user to merge.
Never merge it.

Read [full-send](../full-send/SKILL.md) and follow its workflow, proof rules,
review, and babysitting steps. An explicit "full stop" request authorizes that
work without a separate "full send" request. That includes full-send's
testing permission. A "full stop" request is the permission for the test
methods Proof needs, even when a project file says to ask first, for
example before computer use. Use those methods directly. Its merge
permission does not apply. The overrides below take precedence.

## No merging

You may commit, push, rebase, fix conflicts, and use `--force-with-lease` on
this task's branch. Never merge, enable auto-merge, enter a merge queue, push
to the default branch, bypass branch protection, or delegate those actions.

Disable existing auto-merge and remove the PR from any merge queue before
work begins; check again before each push. Report these changes. If you
cannot prevent automatic merging, report the blocker before proceeding.

## Stop at the gate

Use full-send's merge gate as the readiness check. Replace its merge and
final report steps with a handoff. Proof and review must cover the final diff;
recheck behavior changes and meaningful conflict fixes before handoff.

Fetch the target branch and check the live PR's head, base, checks, reviews,
and mergeability. Confirm it is open, not a draft, and not set to merge
without the user. If someone else merged it, report that instead.

- **Ready to merge:** the merge gate passes. Leave the PR open and unmerged.
- **Waiting for required approval:** only human approval remains. Confirm
  that this is the actual blocker.
- **Blocked:** explain what prevents readiness, what you tried, and what is
  needed. Follow full-send's rules for asking the user.

In T3 Code, call `unwatch_pull_request` before the handoff or a question.
Report the PR link, final head, verdict, proof, reviewer outcome, and remaining
risks. State whether the PR is still open and unmerged.

# smol-loop

This is a workflow for making your code changes more correct before (or
sometimes after) filing a pull request. tl;dr - use subagents to review
your code in a loop.

Make the most minimal possible changes to appease the "minion" reviewers. Be careful
of scope creep and don't be scared to push back.

"Minion(s)" = GPT 6 Luna or Haiku 5.5 models

GPT models are generally better at backend work, computer use/browser use, and being somewhat thourghough while Haiku is generally better(somewhat) at UI and writing cleaner, nicer to maintain code. Take this with a pinch of salt but don't waste your time trying to test out each model for every task and round you do because that's frivolous.

## Budget

- Default: 3 rounds total. Round 1 is full. Later rounds check only
  changed code and open findings.
- Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or
  state/concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open with evidence. Or when
  the user asks.
- Stop early if a round returns only nits. Declined nits and comment,
  doc, or format-only fixes need no new round.
- One reviewer only. "Minions" must not start subagents or reviewers.
- Keep a ledger: id, severity, outcome, usage if returned. Never guess it.

## 1. Scope

Run `git status --short`. Do not stash, discard, or include unrelated
changes. Limit review to the change paths if they separate cleanly.
Otherwise stop and ask.

Find the base after `git fetch origin`:

- PR: `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,headRefOid`. Check out the branch
  only if clean. Confirm `HEAD` is the PR head, or ahead only by this
  change. Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`.
- Local: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. No remote: a base
  the user names, or `HEAD` for uncommitted changes only.

The change is base to working tree in those paths, with untracked files.
Use one diff command all rounds. State intent and out-of-scope in 1-2
sentences. Run covering checks. Do not send code this change breaks. Note
missing or pre-failing checks in the brief.

## 2. Start a "minion"

In T3, call `orchestrator_capabilities`. Pick the latest "minion" model unless the user
named a version. Do not hardcode an ID. Record provider, model, and effort
only if exposed. Use `delegate_task` every round (`role: "review"`,
`mode: "async"`). Save `taskId`. New `clientRequestId` per round.
`childThreadId` is storage, not the next target. Do not use
`t3_thread_send`, `create_threads`, or `t3_thread_launch` for review.

If T3 tools are not listed, try one direct capability call. Outside T3, use
a native "minion" subagent and keep its ID. In Claude Code, use a custom subagent
only if it is set up to run "minion". If no route runs "minion", report the blocker. Do
not substitute a model.

Do not edit scoped files while review runs. Wait for the notice. Do not
poll or start a second reviewer. Timeout, error, or no reply is not
approval. On failure, cancel, verify stop, restart with the ledger.

Round 1 brief (T3 children get no history):

```
Review only. Do not edit, commit, push, comment on PRs, or start subagents.
Repo: <abs path> Base: <sha> Intent: <intent> Out of scope: <scope> Checks: <results>
See: git diff <base> [-- <paths>]; git status --short (read untracked).
Read surrounding code. Find bugs, broken callers, mismatch with intent.
Skip style unless it hides a bug. Hold to the smallest change. Flag code,
tests, or guards the intent does not need. Other paths, rare cases, small
perf, extra compat: nits.
blocker = intended case wrong. should = real bug callers will hit, in intent. nit = rest.
Reply:
VERDICT: APPROVE or CHANGES
S1 [blocker|should|nit] <file>:<line> <claim>. Fix: <suggestion> (stable ids)
```

## 3. Answer findings

Check each finding and severity yourself. Another path, rare case, or
small cost is a nit, whatever label it came with.

- Agree: smallest fix. Prefer delete or narrow over new lock, cache,
  helper, or option. Fix the case that happened. Add one focused test
  that fails without the fix, if intent needs it.
- Disagree: say why, with evidence (file:line, test, output).
- Out of scope or nit: decline in one line. List as follow-up.

Update the ledger. Re-run checks and `git diff --shortstat <base>`. If
review grew the diff, cut first. Do not agree just to end the loop.

## 4. Next round

Start one only if budget remains and a blocker or should is open, behavior code
changed, or approval does not cover the current behavior diff. Use a fresh
`delegate_task` in T3, or follow up the saved native ID. Send the round 1 brief,
the ledger (`fixed:` / `disagree:` / `declined:` + evidence), the same base
diff, and the change since last round. Tell the "minion": open ids and changed code only.
Mark each old id `resolved` or `still open: <reason>`.

## 5. Stop and ship

Agreed: APPROVE on the current behavior diff, no blocker or should open,
no concern of your own. Stuck: an item stays disputed after two replies,
or budget ends. Show both sides in 2-3 lines each. The user decides.
Budget end is not approval.

Do not push during the loop. Push after agreement only if the user asked
to push, ship, or update the PR. If you push to a PR, add above the model
blurb:

`Reviewed with smol-loop: <N> rounds with <model>. Minion verdict: approved`.

Add `on <effort>` only if verified.

Report: rounds, model, what the "minion(s)" changed, diff size before/after, fixed and
declined findings with reasons, usage if exposed (else say not), pushed or not.

# Full Stop

Do the same work as `full-send`, but stop with the PR ready for the user to merge.
Never merge it.

Read [full-send](../full-send/SKILL.md) and follow its workflow, proof rules,
review, and babysitting steps. An explicit "full stop" request authorizes that
work without a separate "full send" request. That includes full-send's
testing permission. A "full stop" request is the permission for the test
methods Proof needs, even when a project file says to ask first, for
example before computer use. Use those methods directly. Its merge
permission does not apply. The overrides below take precedence.

## No merging

You may commit, push, rebase, fix conflicts, and use `--force-with-lease` on
this task's branch. Never merge, enable auto-merge, enter a merge queue, push
to the default branch, bypass branch protection, or delegate those actions.

Disable existing auto-merge and remove the PR from any merge queue before
work begins; check again before each push. Report these changes. If you
cannot prevent automatic merging, report the blocker before proceeding.

## Stop at the gate

Use full-send's merge gate as the readiness check. Replace its merge and
final report steps with a handoff. Proof and review must cover the final diff;
recheck behavior changes and meaningful conflict fixes before handoff.

Fetch the target branch and check the live PR's head, base, checks, reviews,
and mergeability. Confirm it is open, not a draft, and not set to merge
without the user. If someone else merged it, report that instead.

- **Ready to merge:** the merge gate passes. Leave the PR open and unmerged.
- **Waiting for required approval:** only human approval remains. Confirm
  that this is the actual blocker.
- **Blocked:** explain what prevents readiness, what you tried, and what is
  needed. Follow full-send's rules for asking the user.

In T3 Code, call `unwatch_pull_request` before the handoff or a question.
Report the PR link, final head, verdict, proof, reviewer outcome, and remaining
risks. State whether the PR is still open and unmerged.

input.task:
Role: review only. Do not read files, run commands, edit anything, or use tools. Judge from this description alone, and say where you would want a claim checked before acting on it.

Context: inkling is a Windows Electron desktop app: a React/TypeScript renderer, a Node main process with SQLite, and Effect 4 in the main process. Project rules that matter here: capture must never block on processing; full content must not cross Electron IPC (summaries and thumbnails only); the card grid is virtualized; fetched HTML is untrusted and sanitized; Effect lives only in the main process (one renderer exception, src/lib/ingestion/http.ts); no hardcoded localhost ports or user paths; a logic bug needs a failing test before its fix; prefer the smallest change, and treat rare cases, extra compatibility, and small performance costs as nits. The maintainer does not want scope creep or machinery for its own sake.

Source: a read-only audit by SWE-2 of branch t3/quick-wins-audit, base commit 0e40de9. Goal: small, low-risk fixes that can land now without a product decision.

Already changed in the working tree. Judge each as KEEP or REVERT:
F1. update_item wrote the sourceUrl field with no validation. The other write paths (saveUrl, createQuote, captureUrl) validate it with normalizeHttpUrl. The change: update validates the same way when sourceUrl is provided. Null leaves the stored value alone; an empty string now errors. A regression test was added that fails without the fix.
F2. The reader view rendered the stored sourceUrl as a link href with no scheme check, so a stored javascript: value would be clickable. The change: the footer link renders only for http and https URLs. This was found while verifying the audit, not by the audit itself.
F3. Extension badge: the success timer after a save was never cancelled, so a second save within 1.4 seconds could have its badge cleared early by the first save's timer. The change: cancel the pending timer before arming a new one.
F4. Copy: six places (the extension options page, its script, the background error message, the extension README twice, and STORE.md) say "Settings → Extension". The app's tab is labeled "Browser extension". The change: copy only.
F5. Dead module: packages/ingestion-shared/src/defuddle-config.ts exported DEFUDDLE_VERSION_PIN ("0.19.3", while the root dependency is ^0.19.5) and INKLING_DEFUDDLE_OPTIONS. Nothing imports either. The change: the file was deleted, its re-export removed, the package's own defuddle dependency removed (the root still has it), the lockfile workspace entry updated, and the package description updated.

Open, not changed yet:
O1 [performance, medium size]. Every card-list query (active items, search, Smart Space results) selects the full metadata column. For articles that includes the full extracted HTML and text, and the code parses it for every row. Cards keep only 8 metadata fields, plus a palette and a has-article-content flag. The fix would be one shared alias map that both renderer and backend import, plus a backend test that a Smart Space query with kind `url` returns articles. 8. **O3: NEEDS DECISION.** Question: "Should cards show video duration, file size and reading time? If so, should we add producers now, or delete the fields and their UI until then?" My default is to delete all three, with the contract fields and the card read sites removed in one change. `readingMinutes` would be the cheapest to bring back later, from the extracted word count. Check `docs/product.md` and the design docs first: if they promise any of these, that changes the answer. 9. **O4: NEEDS DECISION.** Question: "Is selection, image or video capture from the extension on the current roadmap?" My default is to delete the mappers, their payload types and their test, since git history keeps them. First confirm that `capture-server.ts` doesn't validate those payload variants. If it does, removing the types would loosen its validation or break it. 10. **O5: FIX NOW.** Delete `src/lib/ingestion/asset-paths.ts` and its smoke test, and fix the ingestion README line. No failing test is needed. Before deleting, check that storage's own path code has its own containment tests, so this smoke test isn't the only containment check. It could break nothing if typecheck and knip pass. 11. **O6: NIT.** It only affects the dev web preview with sample data, and the leak goes away on reload. 12. **O7: NEEDS DECISION.** Question: "Should HEIC and SVG be image items, which needs decode or rasterize support for thumbnails, OCR and embeddings, or file items?" My default is one shared extension list: - HEIC and HEIF become files, because Chromium can't decode them. - SVG becomes an image only if it is always shown through `` or a rasterized thumbnail, never opened in a frame or window where its scripts would run. - ICO becomes an image. - WMV becomes a file. - Before choosing for OGV, check whether Chromium still plays Theora. 13. **O8: FIX NOW, with the forgiving default.** On import, run each `source_url` through `normalizeHttpUrl`. If it fails, keep the item and set the URL to null. Don't reject the archive, since losing a user's items is worse than losing a bad link. Test first: import an archive with a `javascript:` `source_url`, then assert the item exists and its `sourceUrl` is null. Possible downside: a hand-edited archive with a non-http link silently loses it. That is acceptable. 14. **O9: NIT.** The path is relative to the home folder rather than an absolute user path, and it's benchmark scratch. Fix it only if someone touches the script anyway. **Overstated or misdescribed** - F2 says the stored value is "found while verifying" and "clickable". How bad that is depends on whether the renderer has a navigation guard (`will-navigate` or `setWindowOpenHandler`) and whether the link goes through `openExternal`. Check both to size it correctly. Either way, it is still the right fix. - O1 calls option (a) a full blob read. That is true for `json_extract` on the metadata column. But if a column is simply left out of the SELECT, SQLite can usually skip that column's overflow pages. So "(a) still reads the blob" depends on which form of (a) is used. - O1 calls the change "medium size". That understates (b) (see item 6). - O2's "only imported or hand-written queries" is unverified (see item 7). - O3's "never passed to cards" should also be checked against the preview seed data. If the seed data supplies these fields, they show up in preview. - "Scoped checks pass" refers to `check:changed` only. That's fine, but say so in the PR body. **Missing from the list** - **Other places `sourceUrl` is used.** "Open original" in the card or detail view, any context-menu "copy or open link", and above all the main process's `shell.openExternal` handler. The http/https allowlist belongs in the main process too, not only in one footer link. If it's missing there, that is the most important fix on this branch. - **Changelog.** F2, and F1 together with it, deserve one Security line in `docs/changelog.md`. - **F1 normalizing.** If `normalizeHttpUrl` rewrites URLs (trailing slash, lowercasing), editing an unrelated field now silently rewrites a stored URL. Check that update only normalizes when the URL actually changed, or accept that behavior on purpose. - **F1's reverse state.** With `null` meaning "no change" and `""` an error, a user can no longer clear a source URL. That's probably fine, but it's a one-way door. Name it.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\chris\.claude\skills\full-send

# Full Send

If the user triggered this, it's because they are not watching this thread, and
they want you to complete the work end-to-end autonomously. Your updates and
your final message go unread until long after you stop. You own the work from
its current state to a merged PR.

If the user did not explicitly request "full send" in some clear way, do not
assume full autonomy. If they did, everything below applies.

The user grants you permission to:

- Merge the PR once the merge gate passes.
- Force-push the PR's own branch with `--force-with-lease` after a rebase.
- Use the test methods that Proof needs, without asking first.

## Testing permission

A "full send" request is the permission. If a project file or other
instruction says to ask before a test method, or to leave testing to the
user, this request replaces that rule for this task.

That includes ask-first rules for computer use, browser automation,
simulators and devices, running the app or a dev server, screenshots, and
visual checks. Use the method that gives direct proof. List it in the
report.

Rules about how to test still apply. Follow rules that name the correct
command, fixture, or check. This permission only removes the ask-first or
leave-it-to-the-user step. If a preferred method cannot prove the change,
use a gated method under this permission.

It covers only the tests needed for this task. It does not add permission
for the steps under "Asking the user", such as production changes or data
deletion. It also does not bypass a harness or system approval prompt if
one appears.

## Steps

1. **Finish the change.** Complete the goal from the user's request with the
   smallest change that works. Fix the case that happened, not every case
   that could. If you are on the default branch, create a branch first.
2. **Prove it.** Get proof for every change you made. See "Proof".
3. **Get feedback.** Use the `smol-loop` skill to verify changes.
4. **File the PR** with the `file-pr` skill. Rebase onto the latest default
   branch first. Add one short line to the description that says how you proved
   the change.
5. **Babysit the PR** with the `babysit-pr` skill. Fix real findings and CI
   failures. Get proof for each fix before you push it.
6. **Merge** when the merge gate passes.
7. **Report** in your final message: the PR link, the merge commit, your proof,
   and each decision you made for the user.

Stay active from step 1 to step 7. If you end your turn while checks or bots are
pending, the work stops, because nobody will prompt you again. Wait with the
watcher from `babysit-pr`, so something wakes you when the PR changes. In T3
Code that is `watch_pull_request`. If you stop before the merge, call
`unwatch_pull_request` first.

## Proof

Proof is evidence you observed yourself in this session: command output, a
reproduction, a screenshot. Use the most direct proof the change allows:

- Reproduce the original failure, apply the fix, then watch the same
  reproduction pass.
- Run the checks that the repo's CI runs (typecheck, lint, tests).
- Add one focused test that fails without the fix, when the behavior has none
  and the repo has a test setup.
- For UI and runtime behavior, run the app and look at the change. Green mocked
  tests do not prove that the user experience works. Attach screenshots to the
  PR when they help and you have a way to upload them.

When you cannot find a way to prove a change, you do not have full confidence.
Ask the user.

## Merge gate

Full confidence means all of these are true on the latest commit:

- Your proof covers every change in the diff.
- Required checks are green.
- Review bots have finished, and each finding is fixed or dismissed with a
  written reason.
- No human review still requests changes.
- The branch is up to date with the default branch, and GitHub reports it as
  mergeable.

Merge with the method the repo uses. Check the allowed methods and recent merged
PRs. If the repo uses a merge queue or auto-merge, stay until GitHub reports the
PR as merged. Merge through branch protection as configured. Never use `--admin`
or other bypasses. You can ignore automated reviews that request "needs human
review" if you have high confidence in your changes.

## Asking the user

A question in a normal message goes unseen, and the thread looks done. To ask
the user something, use the harness's question tool so the thread shows that
it is waiting: `AskUserQuestion` in Claude Code, `request_user_input` in Codex,
or the question tool your harness has. Put all the context in the question:
the PR link, what blocks you, and the options with your recommendation first.

Ask only when you cannot continue alone:

- You cannot prove the change.
- The merge gate cannot pass, and you cannot fix that yourself.
- The next step is outside the grant above: deleting data, touching production,
  changing things outside the repo, closing a PR, or force-pushing any other
  branch.
- The goal is ambiguous in a way that changes the result.
- Another PR makes this one obsolete.

Decide everything else yourself with sensible defaults, and list those decisions
in the report.

If no question tool is available, or the tool returns no answer, take the safe
path: leave the PR open and unmerged, and start your final message with the
question.

input.title: Opus 5.5 triage of audit findings
input.task:
Role: review only. Do not read files, run commands, edit anything, or use tools. Judge from this description alone, and say where you would want a claim checked before acting on it.

Context: inkling is a Windows Electron desktop app: a React/TypeScript renderer, a Node main process with SQLite, and Effect 4 in the main process. Project rules that matter here: capture must never block on processing; full content must not cross Electron IPC (summaries and thumbnails only); the card grid is virtualized; fetched HTML is untrusted and sanitized; Effect lives only in the main process (one renderer exception, src/lib/ingestion/http.ts); no hardcoded localhost ports or user paths; a logic bug needs a failing test before its fix; prefer the smallest change, and treat rare cases, extra compatibility, and small performance costs as nits. The maintainer does not want scope creep or machinery for its own sake.

Source: a read-only audit by SWE-2 of branch t3/quick-wins-audit, base commit 0e40de9. Goal: small, low-risk fixes that can land now without a product decision.

Already changed in the working tree. Judge each as KEEP or REVERT:
F1. update_item wrote the sourceUrl field with no validation. The other write paths (saveUrl, createQuote, captureUrl) validate it with normalizeHttpUrl. The change: update validates the same way when sourceUrl is provided. Null leaves the stored value alone; an empty string now errors. A regression test was added that fails without the fix.
F2. The reader view rendered the stored sourceUrl as a link href with no scheme check, so a stored javascript: value would be clickable. The change: the footer link renders only for http and https URLs. This was found while verifying the audit, not by the audit itself.
F3. Extension badge: the success timer after a save was never cancelled, so a second save within 1.4 seconds could have its badge cleared early by the first save's timer. The change: cancel the pending timer before arming a new one.
F4. Copy: six places (the extension options page, its script, the background error message, the extension README twice, and STORE.md) say "Settings → Extension". The app's tab is labeled "Browser extension". The change: copy only.
F5. Dead module: packages/ingestion-shared/src/defuddle-config.ts exported DEFUDDLE_VERSION_PIN ("0.19.3", while the root dependency is ^0.19.5) and INKLING_DEFUDDLE_OPTIONS. Nothing imports either. The change: the file was deleted, its re-export removed, the package's own defuddle dependency removed (the root still has it), the lockfile workspace entry updated, and the package description updated.

Open, not changed yet:
O1 [performance, medium size]. Every card-list query (active items, search, Smart Space results) selects the full metadata column. For articles that includes the full extracted HTML and text, and the code parses it for every row. Cards keep only 8 metadata fields, plus a palette and a has-article-content flag. The OCR text column is also selected in full, although cards keep only a 180-character snippet. Options: (a) project only the card fields in SQL, which still makes SQLite read the blob; (b) move article bodies to their own column, which needs a migration.
O2 [latent correctness]. Smart Space kind aliases differ. The renderer maps url to article, embed to video, and tweet to post, on both sides of the comparison. The backend expands only "article". The app's UI never writes a kind into a query (it saves text only), so this affects only imported or hand-written queries.
O3 [dead fields]. durationSeconds, fileSizeBytes, and readingMinutes are in the shared contract and read by card UI (video duration, file-size footnote, reading time). They are never passed through to cards and never written by the main process. Options: delete them, or add producers.

# Full Send

If the user triggered this, it's because they are not watching this thread, and
they want you to complete the work end-to-end autonomously. Your updates and

If the user did not explicitly request "full send" in some clear way, do not
assume full autonomy. If they did, everything below applies.

The user grants you permission to:

- Merge the PR once the merge gate passes.
- Force-push the PR's own branch with `--force-with-lease` after a rebase.
- Use the test methods that Proof needs, without asking first.

## Testing permission

A "full send" request is the permission. If a project file or other
instruction says to ask before a test method, or to leave testing to the
user, this request replaces that rule for this task.

That includes ask-first rules for computer use, browser automation,
simulators and devices, running the app or a dev server, screenshots, and
visual checks. Use the method that gives direct proof. List it in the
report.

Rules about how to test still apply. Follow rules that name the correct
command, fixture, or check. This permission only removes the ask-first or
leave-it-to-the-user step. If a preferred method cannot prove the change,
use a gated method under this permission.

It covers only the tests needed for this task. It does not add permission
for the steps under "Asking the user", such as production changes or data
deletion. It also does not bypass a harness or system approval prompt if
one appears.

## Steps

1. **Finish the change.** Complete the goal from the user's request with the
   smallest change that works. Fix the case that happened, not every case
   that could. If you are on the default branch, create a branch first.
2. **Prove it.** Get proof for every change you made. See "Proof".
3. **Get feedback.** Use the `smol-loop` skill to verify changes.
4. **File the PR** with the `file-pr` skill. Rebase onto the latest default
   branch first. Add one short line to the description that says how you proved
   the change.
5. **Babysit the PR** with the `babysit-pr` skill. Fix real findings and CI
   failures. Get proof for each fix before you push it.
6. **Merge** when the merge gate passes.
7. **Report** in your final message: the PR link, the merge commit, your proof,
   and each decision you made for the user.

Stay active from step 1 to step 7. If you end your turn while checks or bots are
pending, the work stops, because nobody will prompt you again. Wait with the
watcher from `babysit-pr`, so something wakes you when the PR changes. In T3
Code that is `watch_pull_request`. If you stop before the merge, call
`unwatch_pull_request` first.

## Proof

Proof is evidence you observed yourself in this session: command output, a
reproduction, a screenshot. Use the most direct proof the change allows:

- Reproduce the original failure, apply the fix, then watch the same
  reproduction pass.
- Run the checks that the repo's CI runs (typecheck, lint, tests).
- Add one focused test that fails without the fix, when the behavior has none
  and the repo has a test setup.
- For UI and runtime behavior, run the app and look at the change. Green mocked
  tests do not prove that the user experience works. Attach screenshots to the
  PR when they help and you have a way to upload them.

When you cannot find a way to prove a change, you do not have full confidence.
Ask the user.

## Merge gate

Full confidence means all of these are true on the latest commit:

- Your proof covers every change in the diff.
- Required checks are green.
- Review bots have finished, and each finding is fixed or dismissed with a
  written reason.
- No human review still requests changes.
- The branch is up to date with the default branch, and GitHub reports it as
  mergeable.

Merge with the method the repo uses. Check the allowed methods and recent merged
PRs. If the repo uses a merge queue or auto-merge, stay until GitHub reports the
PR as merged. Merge through branch protection as configured. Never use `--admin`
or other bypasses. You can ignore automated reviews that request "needs human
review" if you have high confidence in your changes.

## Asking the user

A question in a normal message goes unseen, and the thread looks done. To ask
the user something, use the harness's question tool so the thread shows that
it is waiting: `AskUserQuestion` in Claude Code, `request_user_input` in Codex,
or the question tool your harness has. Put all the context in the question:
the PR link, what blocks you, and the options with your recommendation first.

Ask only when you cannot continue alone:

- You cannot prove the change.
- The merge gate cannot pass, and you cannot fix that yourself.
- The next step is outside the grant above: deleting data, touching production,
  changing things outside the repo, closing a PR, or force-pushing any other

- The goal is ambiguous in a way that changes the result.
- Another PR makes this one obsolete.

Decide everything else yourself with sensible defaults, and list those decisions
in the report.

If no question tool is available, or the tool returns no answer, take the safe

Repo: C:\Users\chris\.t3\worktrees\inkling\t3-92256e78 (branch t3/quick-wins-audit, base commit 0e40de9). The working tree already holds uncommitted changes from earlier in this session. Keep them. Do not revert, stash, commit, push, or create branches.

Read AGENTS.md at the repo root first. Rules that matter for this task:
- Effect lives only in the main process. Before writing any Effect code, read node_modules/effect/AGENTS.md. Use Effect.fnUntraced for reusable functions.
- A logic bug gets a failing test first, then the fix. Prefer extending an existing test or table over adding a new test.
- Default to no comment. Keep at most one line where a comment is needed.
- Do NOT run repo-wide checks: no full bun test, no full tsc, no bun run check, no bun run check:changed (the orchestrator runs that). No dev servers, no Electron, no killing processes, no opening the SQLite library except through the test helpers.
- Targeted commands only (see Proof below).

Already done, do not redo: (a) electron/storage/items.ts update_item validates sourceUrl via normalizeHttpUrl, with a regression test in electron/storage.test.ts named "update_item refuses a source URL that is not HTTP or HTTPS". (b) The extension copy fix ("Settings → Browser extension"). (c) Deletion of packages/ingestion-shared/src/defuddle-config.ts and its dependency. (d) A footer guard in src/ReaderView.tsx, which step 2 moves.

Do these five steps, in order.

1. Extension badge, extension/src/background.ts. In showFailure, call clearTimeout(successResetTimer) before setting the failure badge, so a success timer started earlier cannot clear the "!" badge or reset the failure title. There is no test harness for background.ts. Do not add one.

2. Move the web-URL check out of the component. In src/lib/ingestion/url.ts, export isWebUrl(value: string): boolean. It returns true only when the value parses as an http: or https: URL, and false for everything else, including empty strings and relative paths. Add table rows to the existing describe block in src/lib/ingestion/url.test.ts. Do not create a new test file. Rows: https and http are true; javascript:, data:, file:, ftp:, "", a relative path, and garbage are false. In src/ReaderView.tsx, delete the local isWebUrl function and import the one from ./lib/ingestion/url. Leave the footer condition unchanged.

3. Import normalization, electron/storage/import-library.ts around line 300. An imported item whose source_url is not http or https keeps the item and stores source_url as null. Do not reject the archive. Put the rule in one plain synchronous helper, for example in electron/storage/shared.ts, and make normalizeHttpUrl use the same protocol check so the rule lives in one place. Keep the change minimal. TEST FIRST: in electron/storage.test.ts, add one test near the existing export and restore tests (look at roughly lines 825 to 900 for the helper calls). Create a note, set its source_url to 'javascript:alert(1)' through library.db with a prepared statement, export, restore into a fresh library, and assert that the restored item exists and its sourceUrl is null. Run it, confirm it fails on the current import code, quote the failing line, then fix and confirm it passes.

4. Delete the unused module. Delete src/lib/ingestion/asset-paths.ts. In src/lib/ingestion/ingestion.smoke.ts, remove the import on line 6 and the two assert blocks that use assetRelativePath and sanitizeAssetSegment (around lines 368 to 375). In src/lib/ingestion/README.md, remove the asset-paths.ts bullet. Before deleting, grep the whole repo for asset-paths, assetRelativePath, and sanitizeAssetSegment. Earlier searches found only the smoke file and the README. Stop and report if you find anything else.

5. Changelog, docs/changelog.md. Inside the Unreleased section (it starts at line 27 and ends just before "## Phase 5"), add a "### Security" subsection at the end of that section with exactly one line: "Source links must be HTTP or HTTPS: edits reject other values, imports drop them, and the reader only links web addresses." Do not reorder, rewrite, or touch any other line. Do not mention agents or AI.

Proof, targeted only:
- bun test src/lib/ingestion/url.test.ts
- bun test electron/storage.test.ts (the whole file, about 40 seconds, must be 42 passing: the 41 from before plus the new import test)
- bun run ingest:smoke
- bun run --cwd extension typecheck

Final message, under 400 words:
- Files changed, one line each.
- The exact pass counts for each command above.
- The failing-then-passing evidence for the import test: the failure line before the fix, and the pass after.
- Anything you did not do, and why.

content.thinking:
The minion's verdict is approve with four nits, and since the guidance says to stop early when only nits remain, I should ship it rather than loop again—but I still want to verify each finding myself. The duplicate isWebUrl nit seems like a genuine small smell worth fixing by having normalizeHttpUrl check the protocol directly instead of duplicating logic.

I'll agree to this nit since storage importing from src/lib/ingestion is already an established pattern via ai-jobs.ts, so reverting normalizeHttpUrl to its inline check and reusing the url.ts helper is justified rather than just agreeing to end the loop.

I think I'll settle on reverting normalizeHttpUrl to its original inline check and keeping the electron isWebUrl as string-only, dropping the awkward unknown/instanceof branch. I'll decline the cross-layer import suggestion since storage is the library layer and shouldn't pull in renderer code — the duplicate one-line protocol check is an acceptable tradeoff, but I'll take the small cleanup win on normalizeHttpUrl.

That settles S1: decline the cross-layer import but keep the revert of normalizeHttpUrl since that's just undoing unnecessary churn.

Now for S2, the "Open host" button in ItemActionBar calls window.open for any truthy sourceUrl, but since the main process already blocks non-http schemes via setWindowOpenHandler, the button is just a no-op for bad URLs rather than a security hole. Gating it with isWebUrl would be a cheap, consistent 1-line fix even though it's a rare edge case, so I lean toward agreeing for consistency with the reader fix — then I need to check useCardMenu.ts too.

I'm now noticing useCardMenu.ts has the exact same window.open pattern on its "Open original" menu item, which the minion missed — if I gate ItemActionBar I should gate this too, but that's scope creep since the main-process handler already blocks the dangerous scheme everywhere. This makes me question whether the ReaderView link guard is even necessary, since that href's click also routes through the same window-open handler via target=_blank — though its real purpose is preventing a javascript: href from ever sitting in the DOM at all, which is a different justification. I'm settling on declining S2: the main-process handler already denies non-HTTP(S) URLs for every window.open and link target, so gating these individual buttons would just duplicate that protection redundantly.

For S3, the background timer lacks a regression test, and AGENTS requires tests for behavior changes — but there's no browser-API test harness and faking browser.action/timers would require real machinery, which seems disproportionate for what's really just a two-line clearTimeout pair; I'm leaning toward declining with that justification rather than building a harness.

But I'm reconsidering since the AGENTS rule explicitly says to flag exceptions and get sign-off rather than silently skip them, and the repo already has a test setup (capture.test.ts, transport.test.ts), so the proof rule arguably still applies here. The real obstacle is that background.ts triggers side effects on import like registering onInstalled listeners, so testing it means mocking webextension-polyfill globally — which other extension tests presumably already handle somehow.

Rather than relying on fake timers, I could manually override setTimeout/clearTimeout in the test to capture and trigger callbacks by hand, verifying the success timer gets cleared on failure. That's a legitimate behavior-focused test rather than a mock-call mirror, since it checks observable badge state rather than just asserting a function was called.

I'll route this to SWE-2 to add the test, since the user wants everything fixed and the module mocking should work fine with bun's test runner against webextension-polyfill. There's a related race concern — a success timer armed after awaits could clobber a failure badge that occurs during those awaits — but that requires two rapid saves and I'm inclined to decline fixing it as out of scope unless it's trivial.

Actually there's a zero-cost fix: just move the clearTimeout/arm call before the awaits in showSuccess, so a concurrent failure's clearTimeout would properly cancel the newly-armed timer. Since that's a simple reorder with no real cost, I'll accept it and apply it.

For S1, I'll agree to revert normalizeHttpUrl to its original inline check, keep electron's helper string-only, but decline the cross-layer import suggestion — reduces unnecessary diff while staying in scope. S2 stays declined with evidence given, and S3 gets rolled into SWE-2's work as a focused background test.

Round 1 comes back as APPROVE with only nits, but since S4's timer-arming reorder and S1's revert both touch actual behavior code, the loop rule says I need to start a second review round on just the changed code — I've got 2 of 3 rounds left, so this is within budget even if it feels like marginal overhead.

For the SWE-2 fix batch: I'm reverting normalizeHttpUrl in shared.ts to its original inline protocol check, simplifying isWebUrl to take only a string, and updating the import-library call to null out source_url only when it's non-empty and not a web URL. The rest of ReaderView and url.ts stay untouched, and now I'm looking at what background.ts's showSuccess needs.

I'm moving the clearTimeout and timer arming to the top before the badge awaits, per S4. For S3, I'm designing a new background.test.ts that mocks webextension-polyfill, simulates a success followed by a failure, and confirms the stale success-reset timer firing afterward doesn't clobber the failure badge still showing "!" — verifying this fails on the pre-fix code first, then restoring the fix. I'm sketching the mock shape needed for browser.action, runtime, contextMenus, storage, and tabs, and working out how to await the real async flow (via a deferred resolved on the badge-set call) rather than polling, since the onClicked listener fires a detached async save without returning a promise. I decide the test is worth the complexity given the review rules, and note SWE-2 should flag it rather than force it if the mocking becomes unmanageable, while not expanding background.ts beyond the simple reorder.

I'm compiling the ledger of outcomes across all four review items — one reverted, one declined with evidence from main.ts's setWindowOpenHandler, one to be fixed via the new test, one via the timer reorder — and confirming my decline on S2 is grounded in already-seen code rather than the minion's unverified claim about Electron's ingestion import. Now I'm drafting the brief for SWE-2 max: pass along the ledger, scope the changed files, specify the fail-first test verification step, state the check commands (noting bun test from root should pick up extension tests via default discovery), and explicitly tell it not to touch ReaderView, ItemActionBar, or useCardMenu.

The minion approved round 1 with four nits, and it did not raise any blocker or should. I checked each one against the code:

I'm declining the cross-layer import from storage into the renderer's ingestion code, since storage is the library layer. The remaining duplicate is a few lines.

- **S4 (timer armed after the awaits):** Agreed. Moving the arm to the start of `showSuccess` is free and closes the race.

conventions. Look at recently merged PRs and Git history for examples. Prefer a
concise, human-readable title that explains why the change matters:

BAD

> ❌ perf(server): negotiate permessage-deflate on the websocket

GOOD

> ✅ perf(server): cut websocket frame size by 70%+ with gzipping

Open the description with a simple explanation of the problem based on the
user's original prompt, then briefly explain the solution. Do not lead with an
implementation inventory:

BAD

> ❌ Removed implicit workspace carry-over from every "new thread" entry point (cmd+n / cmd+shift+o, sidebar v1/v2 buttons, command palette). New threads inherit only the project from context; branch, worktree, and env mode always come from the configured defaults. Deleted buildContextualThreadOptions, startNewThreadInProjectFromContext, and the v1 sidebar's seed-context machinery.

GOOD

> ✅ My "new worktree" default was ignored when starting new threads on existing worktrees. Super unintuitive. Now your preferences always apply.

End the description with the public model name and harness that made the
changes, for example `Created with <model> in <harness>.` Include subagent
models that wrote part of the change. Use the model name the harness reports.
If model identity is unavailable, name the harness without guessing a model.

Before submission, check the title, description, quotes, and attachments for
secrets and private details.

Open a real PR rather than a draft so review bots run. If `gh pr create` fails
because the GraphQL rate limit is used up, open it through REST with
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls -f title=... -f head=... -f base=... -F body=@<file>`. If the user also asked
to babysit it, continue with the `babysit-pr` skill.

Do not post a follow-up PR comment unless it serves the user's request. When a

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.

# inkling

inkling is a home for everything worth keeping. Articles, images, screenshots, PDFs, notes, quotes, video links. An Electron desktop app for Windows, with React, TypeScript, and Vite in the frontend and Node.js and SQLite in the backend. Everything stays on the machine.

Think of it as a private visual library with semantic search as the only organizer. No folders to maintain. Save arbitrary media in seconds, find it later by describing it.

## What makes inkling special

People keep things here they do not want to lose, things that are important to them, or that give them inspiration or creative ideas. These are the things that we must never compromise on.

### 1. Capture is instant and seamless

Saving must be faster than deciding where something belongs. The card appears right away. OCR, embeddings, fetching and/or indexing run in the background while the user keeps browsing or continues on with something else. A change that blocks capture on processing is a bug, no matter how correct the processing is.

### 2. Performance

Lots of apps have gotten bogged down with bad tech decisions and "slop". We regularly audit for performance regressions, often caused by passing full content over Electron IPC instead of summaries/thumbnails, rendering the card grid without virtualization, loading full assets where a thumbnail would do, blocking capture on extraction/OCR/embeddings, and running FTS + vector + Smart Space re-evaluation on every keystroke. Keep capture instant and processing in background jobs. Make sure all changes are considerate of performance impact.

### 3. Local first, forever

The library lives in SQLite on the user's disk, with files kept as assets beside it under `assets/items/<id>/`. No account, no feed, no tracking. Network is only for fetching data in a URL the user asked to save like video embed links, the one time model download, or when a user plays a video embed link but that is handled by the embed. Do not add calls home, analytics, or silent uploads.

### 4. Quiet intelligence

AI helpers stay invisible. They make search better. Never surface confidence scores, AI labels, tag correction flows, or model management chores in the main interface. Never rewrite a user title, note, or tag. When AI fails, fall back to plain metadata and text search. Our mascot is an ink-blot that stays out of the way. Calm at rest, subtly alive while work runs, sad only when capture fails. It never talks, never explains AI, never interrupts, it just chills in the background and gives some life to the app.

### 5. Visual by type

An article, a photo, a PDF, a quote and a note should not all look like generic bookmarks. Each media type gets its own card treatment and its own thumbnail. Keep it that way when adding types.

## A note on taste

Simple software that feels obvious beats impressive machinery. Do not preserve complexity just because it already exists. Do not introduce machinery because it looks architecturally impressive. Understand the real constraint, then fight for the smallest model that makes the correct behavior unsurprising.

Channel both "measure twice, cut once" and "yagni". Fight scope creep. Try to honor the dev's intent in both a minimal and realistic fashion.

The rest of this document is meant to help you navigate the codebase and make changes effectively. Think of these instructions less as "hard rules", more as "good defaults". The developer's preferences should be able to override anything here. Most work in this repo will be done by agents, sometimes remote. Be careful with data, dev servers, and anything that could damage the session you are working from.

If a rule here fights the task in front of you, say so plainly and get a human sign off before breaking it.

## Glossary

We need to be on the same page with terminology. When communicating, use this language:

- **you** means the agent reading this file and changing inkling.
- **we and maintainers** mean the people building inkling. That is who you are talking to now.
- **user** means the person using inkling, saving things and searching them later.
- **item** means one saved thing in the library, whatever its type. Data, not UI.
- **card** means how an item looks in the grid and in detail. UI, not data.
- **library** means the SQLite database plus the asset store on disk.
- **capture** means getting something into the library. Paste a URL, pick a file, drag in, paste from clipboard, screenshot, or deep link.
- **job** means one unit of background work. OCR, extraction, embeddings, indexing. Runs on a persisted queue with leases.
- **embedding** means the local vector for text or image search. Nomic text and vision share one 768-dimension space.
- **Space** means a saved search shown as a collection. Smart Spaces update themselves. Regular Spaces hold manually user curated items.
- **deep link** means the companion path into the app, `inkling://capture?url=...`.
- **preview** means `bun run dev`, the web-only look with sample data.
- **full app** means the Windows Electron desktop app with the real library, built with `bun run build:dir` or `bun run build:installer`.

## The three ways to hurt yourself

1. **Killing by pattern.** Never `pkill -f`, `pgrep | kill`, or `kill` a PID you found by matching a name, path, or worktree string. Your own agent process has this worktree's path in its argv, and this machine runs several other dev servers at once. Kill only a PID you captured at spawn, or the owner of your port after confirming it is your worktree (`Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen` and the `Win32_Process` command line on Windows, `ss -H -ltnp` and `/proc/<pid>/cwd` on Linux).

2. **Writing to the live library.** The developer's real data is the SQLite file and asset store the running app owns. Reading it is fine. Copying from it for test fixtures is good. Never start a server against it, never open it read-write, never clean it up.

3. **Baking in local paths and ports.** Never hardcode a localhost port, an absolute user path, or a machine specific model cache path into source or committed config. Preview and the full app must keep working from a fresh clone on another Windows machine. Never commit a database file, a model artifact, a downloaded embedding, or a benchmark output besides the two tracked files. Never commit a pairing secret, token, or full capture URL with real content.

## Hit every surface

The common defect here is a change that works on the path tested and is missing everywhere else. Before calling ingestion or display work done, walk this list and name the entries that applied; skip the rest silently.

- **Entry points.** A behavior reachable from the Add button is usually also reachable from paste, drag and drop, clipboard, screenshot capture, and the deep link. Fixing one is not fixing the feature.
- **Capture paths.** URL, article extraction, image file, screenshot, PDF, note, quote, video link, X post, misc file. An extractor change needs a decision per path, even if the decision is not supported here.
- **Search paths.** Titles, notes, article text, OCR text, domains, authors, manual tags, derived concepts, colors, semantic similarity, dates, types. If you index a new field, say how search reaches it.
- **Card types.** Article, image, PDF, video, post, note, quote, and file, as the `ItemKind` union in `src/lib/types.ts`. Shared thumbnail logic lives in one place. Keep the set coherent.
- **Reverse states.** If you added a way in, add the way out and a way to see it. Trash needs restore. A Space needs rename and delete that keeps its items. A one way door is a bug.
- **App modes.** Preview and the full app behave differently. OCR, embeddings, and file access only run in the Electron app. Do not ship a feature that silently does nothing in one mode.
- **Docs.** Check whether the change makes existing guidance inaccurate. Apply the [documentation rules](#documentation) before adding anything.

## Dev servers

- `bun install` installs. If module resolution looks broken, run `bun run check:bun-version`.
- `bun run dev` is the quick web look at the UI. It uses sample data and has no desktop storage or processing backend.
- `bun run dev:app` opens the Electron shell in preview mode. The renderer shows the sample library and does not call the desktop backend, so capture, OCR, embeddings, and local file access are not exercised there. Test the full backend with the packaged output of `bun run build:dir`.
- `t3.json` lists the T3 Code run scripts. Keep it up to date: whenever a package.json script is renamed or removed, or a command it runs changes, update `t3.json` in the same change.
- Ports and state come from the dev setup, not from memory. Read the actual terminal output. Do not assume a port.
- Stop what you started, by the handle you tracked. See rule 1.
- Never `Start-Sleep` (or any blocking wait) after launching a server. Start it detached, do other work, then poll its log or port. A sleep blocks you from doing anything else while you wait.

## Test data

An empty library is a bad test. Seed your run with a copy of real data instead of pointing at live state.

- Copy the database file with SQLite backup semantics so the copy is consistent even if the source app is open. A raw file copy of a live database is a corrupt copy. Bring the `-wal` and `-shm` siblings when you copy raw, or better, back up through the engine.
- Data flows one way. Into your sandbox, never back out. Copy in, never symlink. Never write your test edits back to the source.
- Bring assets only for the items your flow needs. Do not copy the whole asset store to test one card.
- The committed demo seed in `public/seed-demo/` plus `src/seedPersonal.ts` is the safe default for UI work. It shuffles with a fixed seed so the order is mixed but stable. Prefer it over real data when it covers your case.
- Never commit a copied database, a real user item, or a downloaded model. The gitignore already excludes run artifacts. Keep it that way.

## Verifying

- Smallest proof that the change works. While iterating, `bun test <files>` for the tests you touched. Before pushing, `bun run check:changed`: lint, format, tests, Knip, and typecheck scoped to what the branch changed. The full check is `bun run check`, which mirrors the CI frontend job. Do not run it unless you changed something broad or the user asked.
- **Do not run repo-wide checks.** No full `bun test` sweep or full `tsc` unless asked. CI owns the full suite.
- A test earns its place by guarding something that breaks quietly: extraction and sanitizing, embed allowlists, OCR scoring, queue leases and recovery, migrations and persistence, asset path containment and range requests, deep link and external-format parsing, ordering and race guarantees, and `liquidGlassShape`. A test added with a bug fix stays; mark it `// regression: #NNN` if its name doesn't say so.
- Don't write tests the types already prove, trivial logic, basic DOM behavior, static-markup renders, mock-call mirrors, smoke tests, duplicate table rows, or wall-clock and perf asserts.
- Ingestion and background changes ship with focused tests for that behavior. A behavior change with no test is unfinished.
- Proof for a bug fix depends on the bug. Logic, data, state, and protocol bugs get a failing test first (the fewest that fail on `main` for that reason), then the fix. Purely visual bugs (spacing, colour, alignment, a layout shift) get before/after captures and no test.
- Extend before you add. When an existing test or table covers the behavior, add a row or an assertion there. Write a new `it` only when no case fits. Test at the lowest layer that fails on `main`, not again in a wrapper or at each call site.
- Background work is async. Await the real signal: a job drain, a lease state, an event. No fixed sleeps, per-test timeouts, retries, `Date.now()` or `performance.now()` deltas, polling loops, or skips without a reason.
- UI changes need one real pass in the running app before you call them done (the `verify-inkling` skill drives it). Preview for layout, full app for anything native. Take a screenshot through the harness so the user can see it. The primary agent does this once after integrating. Subagents do not launch their own dev servers. Clean up what you launched when you are done.
- There are no local hooks. CI runs the frontend checks and Electron package smoke tests.

## Pull requests

- Never make a PR unless the developer explicitly asks you to do so.
- Conventional commit titles, plain language: `fix(reader): code blocks keep line breaks`.
- Body: the problem in a sentence or two, then how you fixed it. End with the model and harness that did the work.
- UI changes need before/after images. Motion or timing needs a short video.
- Upload PR evidence to GitHub. Never commit PR-only screenshots or assets such as `.github/pr-assets/`.
- One request is one PR. Split it only when the maintainer asks.

## Linear issues

- One Linear issue owns one task (e.g. `SQU-6`). That issue is the tracker, not a plan file.
- Before starting: read the issue + comments, move it to In Progress, branch from its `gitBranchName`.
- While working: post major progress as issue comments, never rewrite the description. Keep scratch outside the worktree.
- Monitor by reading status + comments only. Don't start work on an issue already In Review unless asked.
- Before finishing: link the PR to the issue at the top of the description before all content, move it to In Review, tick the `roadmap.md` box and add a changelog line referencing the issue ID in the same PR.
- If merged: move the issue to Done.

## Documentation

Most code changes need no docs change. Agents can read the code.

- Product intent lives in `docs/product.md` and `docs/product-behavior.md`. Architecture reasons live in `docs/tech-stack.md`. Standing goes in `docs/roadmap.md`. What changed goes in `docs/changelog.md`. Do not invent a second place for the same fact.
- Before adding a paragraph, ask what a maintainer would get wrong without it. If reading the relevant code answers the question, leave it out.
- Do not document every feature, enumerate fields or methods, narrate control flow, maintain file catalogs, or append PR summaries. Types, tests, and code already record the implementation. The glossary defines shared vocabulary; it is not a feature index.
- Keep a local implementation explanation in a nearby code comment. Use an internal doc when the reasoning crosses boundaries or needs context the code cannot carry well. Link to the relevant source instead of copying it.
- When a documented decision or constraint changes, rewrite or remove the affected text. Do not append another account of the new behavior. A new internal page needs a distinct, durable reason to exist.
- Keep user docs in the shipped product's voice, without implementation details or contributor tooling. Update the relevant feature section when how to use it changes. A UI tweak does not need a documentation entry, and a new control does not need its own page. A settings path is useful; descriptions of visible buttons, icons, layouts, animations, or every UI state are not. Before adding text, ask what task or decision it helps the user with.
- The changelog rules live at the top of `docs/changelog.md` and still apply. One line per entry, grouped under Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed, Deprecated, Security. Trivial edits skip the changelog.
- `docs/operations/` holds maintainer setup, release, and debugging procedures. Keep instructions for operating an installed inkling version in the user guides.

## Plans and work artifacts

- Do not commit implementation plans, research notes, or agent scratch files. Keep temporary working material outside the worktree. `.plans/` is gitignored only as a safety net for legacy tooling.
- Track active maintainer work in its Linear issue (see [Linear issues](#linear-issues)). External proposals follow `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- A merged PR is the implementation record. Do not keep a task checklist in the repository; `docs/roadmap.md` records milestone standing only.

## How it works

Capture creates the item immediately, then background jobs do the slow parts. Normalize, extract text and metadata, run OCR or PDF extraction or article parsing, generate embeddings. Writes to items update the FTS index through triggers. The user keeps browsing or does something else while jobs run. A job can be retried, its lease can expire, and interrupted jobs recover on restart.

Search combines exact FTS over content, notes, and OCR text with semantic similarity over local embeddings. Smart Spaces are saved searches whose query runs each time their items load, so they need no background job.

The Electron main process owns files, the job queue, the database, and model execution. It is written with Effect 4, whose API differs a lot from the Effect 3 most models remember. Before writing or changing Effect code, read `node_modules/effect/AGENTS.md`, `node_modules/effect/ai-docs/`, and the package source instead of relying on memory (run `bun install` if `node_modules` is missing). The renderer gets a narrow preload bridge, not raw filesystem or shell access. Fetched HTML is untrusted. It gets sanitized, embeds pass an allowlist, scripts and event handlers are stripped.

Full reasoning in `docs/tech-stack.md`. Behavior contract in `docs/product-behavior.md`.

## Where code lives

- `src/` is the React and TypeScript frontend. Entry at `src/main.tsx`. Feature code lives in `src/features/` by area (library, item-view, spaces, capture, shell, settings). `src/App.tsx` composes the features, and the reader is `src/ReaderView.tsx`.
- `src/lib/ingestion/` is the capture and extraction pipeline. Defuddle, metadata fallback, sanitizing, video link handling. URL ingestion also runs in Electron's main process (`electron/ai-jobs.ts` imports it).
- `src/components/` holds shared pieces such as the card media (`ItemMedia.tsx`), the liquid glass surfaces, the mascot, and onboarding. `src/ui/` holds shared UI primitives.
- `packages/contracts/` is the IPC contract: the command list and Effect Schemas that preload, main, and renderer share. The renderer calls them through `src/lib/libraryApi.ts`.
- `packages/ingestion-shared/` is the capture payload format and validation shared by the extension and the app.
- `electron/` holds the desktop main process (`main.ts`), preload bridge, PDF/OCR, embeddings, the loopback capture receiver (`capture-server.ts`), and packaging inputs. SQLite schema, storage, and the job queue are in `electron/storage/`.
- `extension/` is the Chrome extension, a capture entry point. It posts to the loopback receiver, or hands the URL to the app through the `inkling://capture` link.
- `scripts/` holds build and check scripts, such as `build-electron.ts` and `assert-command-refs.ts`.
- `benchmarks/` holds the corpus, the harness, expected outputs, and results. Of `benchmarks/results/`, only `results-latest.json` and `summary.md` are tracked.
- `public/seed-demo/` plus `src/seedPersonal.ts` is the committed demo library for UI work.
- `docs/` holds product, behavior, design, models, stack, roadmap, bugs, and changelog. Maintainer procedures live in `docs/operations/`, and `docs/README.md` indexes them.

## Taste

- Complexity belongs at the adapter boundary. Ingestion stays explicit, UI stays dumb.
- Inferred types over annotations. `any` is the enemy.
- Effect lives in the main process and stops at the IPC edge. The one renderer use is `src/lib/ingestion/http.ts` (preview-mode capture); don't add more. Reusable Effect functions use `Effect.fnUntraced`, not `Effect.fn` (nothing collects spans). Keep `Effect.gen` for inline programs and layers.
- Default to no comment. Keep one only where a reader would likely break something without it: a race or ordering guarantee, a security or sanitizing check, a Chromium, Electron, WebGPU or OS quirk, or an invariant another file relies on. One line where you can, four at most. Don't restate names, narrate steps, label sections, record history, explain the fix you just made (the PR carries that), or leave a TODO without an issue. Lint directives, knip tags and license headers stay. `inkling/no-low-value-comments` in `oxlint-plugin-inkling/` enforces the length cap and the mechanical cases, and every `oxlint-disable` needs a `-- reason`.
- Our users should never notice a dropped frame, a lying spinner, and a stale label. No continuously repainting animations (with a slight exception for the mascot); they peg the GPU on high-refresh displays.
- Capture paths stay fast and forgiving. Keep partial results when extraction fails. A URL with a title and domain beats an error card.

## Additional tips

- Security is important, but should not be over-indexed on, especially for dev mode/maintainer-only features. The main threat is untrusted web content rendered locally; `docs/tech-stack.md` says to treat all fetched HTML as untrusted. Keep sanitizing and allowlists strict. Keep dev ergonomics simple.

- [No counters on onboarding mockups](onboarding-mockups-no-chrome.md) — Paper onboarding designs show only what the app would show; no "01 / 04" step counters
- [Onboarding flow direction](onboarding-flow-direction.md) — screen order, favourite screens, mascot big-small-small-big rhythm and peek/eyes ideas
- [Alpha crash reporting decision](alpha-crash-reporting-decision.md) — PostHog crash reports approved, opt-out, US region; overrides the no-telemetry rule for alpha
